title: Calligraphy in the Contemporary Home
excerpt: How a centuries-old script finds new life on the walls of modern interiors.
author: Sumaira Arts

sections.heading: A meeting of old and new
paragraphs: Calligraphy brings movement and meaning into a room. Its flowing lines can sit comfortably beside clean furniture and quiet colours, giving a contemporary space a point of reflection.

sections.heading: Give the lettering room
paragraphs: Choose a wall with enough clear space around the work. A simple frame and restrained neighbouring objects help the script remain the focus.

title: Choosing Art for a Room You Live In
excerpt: Scale, light and colour: a calm way to decide what belongs on your wall.
author: Sumaira Arts

sections.heading: Start with the room
paragraphs: Notice where you spend time and which wall you naturally look towards. Artwork should feel connected to daily life, whether it hangs above a sofa or beside a favourite reading chair.

sections.heading: Try the scale first
paragraphs: Mark the proposed dimensions on the wall with removable paper. View the outline from across the room and from nearby before choosing a size.

title: Inside the Studio
excerpt: From first sketch to finished piece: how a commission comes to life.
author: Sumaira Arts

sections.heading: From a first idea
paragraphs: A studio study starts with a question about mood, colour or movement. Small sketches help explore the idea before it reaches the canvas.

sections.heading: Building the surface
paragraphs: Layers of texture change how light meets the work. Leaving time between stages allows the composition to be reconsidered as it develops.

title: Building a Meaningful Gallery Wall
excerpt: A considered approach to arranging art with balance, rhythm and room to breathe.
author: Sumaira Arts

sections.heading: Find a common thread
paragraphs: A gallery wall feels connected when its works share something: a colour, a subject or a consistent frame. They do not need to match exactly.

sections.heading: Arrange before hanging
paragraphs: Lay the pieces on the floor and try several arrangements. Keep the gaps consistent and let one larger work establish the centre of the group.

title: Texture, Light and the Living Room
excerpt: Why tactile artwork changes character as daylight moves through your space.
author: Sumaira Arts

sections.heading: Watch the light
paragraphs: Texture creates small shadows that shift through the day. A surface that feels quiet in morning light can appear more dramatic under an evening lamp.

sections.heading: Keep lighting gentle
paragraphs: Avoid harsh glare that hides the surface. Try a soft light from the side and check the result from your usual sitting position.

title: The Art of Stillness
excerpt: Creating an interior that feels calm, personal and quietly expressive.
author: Sumaira Arts

sections.heading: Make space for quiet
paragraphs: A calm interior does not have to be empty. One carefully placed artwork can give a room character while leaving enough visual space to rest.

sections.heading: Choose with attention
paragraphs: Look for a palette and rhythm you enjoy returning to. Consider how the artwork relates to the room as a whole, rather than filling every available wall.

title: Choose Scale Before Style
excerpt: A simple guide to finding the right canvas proportion for every wall.
author: Sumaira Arts

sections.heading: Measure the setting
paragraphs: Consider the width of nearby furniture and the height of the ceiling. A small work may feel intimate in a reading corner but become lost above a broad sofa.

sections.heading: Test the proportions
paragraphs: Use a paper template to compare sizes. Leave clear space around the artwork and check that it feels balanced from the main entrance to the room.

title: The Quiet Brilliance of Gold Leaf
excerpt: The traditional process behind the luminous detail in selected studio works.
author: Sumaira Arts

sections.heading: Light on a gilded surface
paragraphs: Gold leaf creates a different effect from flat colour. Its reflections shift with the light, drawing attention to small details and changes in the surface.

sections.heading: Balance the brightness
paragraphs: Give luminous work a quiet setting. Soft lighting and restrained accessories allow the gold to become an accent rather than a source of glare.

title: Collecting Art With Intention
excerpt: How to begin a collection that reflects your story rather than a passing trend.
author: Sumaira Arts

sections.heading: Begin with a connection
paragraphs: The first work in a collection need not follow a trend. Spend time with pieces that hold your attention and consider what you enjoy about them.

sections.heading: Let a collection grow
paragraphs: Keep notes on dimensions, materials and placement. Adding work gradually gives each piece a place in your home and lets your preferences evolve.

title: From Conversation to Commission
excerpt: What to expect when a bespoke work is created around your space and vision.
author: Sumaira Arts

sections.heading: Share the starting point
paragraphs: A commission begins with a conversation about the space and the feeling you want to create. Photographs, wall measurements and colour references can make that conversation more useful.

sections.heading: Agree on the details
paragraphs: Discuss the proposed composition, materials, dimensions and framing before work begins. Clear expectations help turn a personal idea into a coherent finished piece.
